scenes.title: 1949 McGill Page 62 & 1973 Oslo/London Oscilloscope: Coincident A->B Firing Jumping the Hippocampal LTP Curve Up 200%

layout.description: Sunlit high-key neurobiology seminar & physiology studio combining Donald Hebb's open **1949 hardcover *The Organization of Behavior* (opened to Page 62)** on a warm oak desk beside an educational sculpted white **Two-Neuron Synapse Model (Cell A -> Cell B)** and Tim Bliss & Terje Lømo's **1973 LTP Oscilloscope & Graph** showing baseline 100% EPSP leaping up to a sustained **200%+ plateau** after coincident A->B burst timing.

positions.who: Donald O. Hebb (mannequin in 1949 tweed jacket, waistcoat, and pipe-free academic spectacles)
positions.where: standing beside the oak desk pointing from Page 62 of his 1949 book to the sculpted white Cell-A-to-Cell-B synapse model

positions.who: Tim Bliss & Terje Lømo (mannequins in 1973 white lab coats over collared shirts)
positions.where: triggering synchronous A->B stimulation pulses and pointing in triumph as the 1973 hippocampal LTP trace jumps from 100% baseline to a steady 220% plateau

props.name: open 1949 *Organization of Behavior* hardcover ('Page 62 Postulate') & sculpted matte-white A->B Synapse Model
props.period_detail: bridges Hebb's 1949 theoretical leap directly to physical synaptic contact

props.name: 1973 Hippocampal LTP Step-Function Graph ('Baseline 100% -> Coincident Burst -> 220% Sustained Days')
props.period_detail: iconic upward step chart from Bliss & Lømo 1973

actions.verb_sequence: test Input A alone (flat 100% baseline) -> trigger coincident A-fires-B burst -> postsynaptic oscilloscope wave and wall graph leap to 220% and hold rock-steady!
nods warmly seeing his 24-year-old page-62 prediction come alive on the trace

reactions.reaction: celebrate physiological proof of mammalian synaptic memory
gestures to the causal 'A takes part in firing B' arrow

scenes.wardrobe: 1949 Canadian tweed three-piece academic suit; 1973 British/Norwegian white laboratory coats over Oxford shirts.
scenes.recognition_hook: In 1949 he guessed it before anyone had seen a synapse; in 1973 one coincident burst sent the hippocampal memory line shooting up 200% for days.

key_visual.description: a sunlit neurobiology bench pairing an open 1949 book and matte-white two-neuron A-to-B synapse sculpture with a 1973 hippocampal LTP graph jumping from 100% baseline to a sustained 220% plateau

scenes.title: The 20-Millisecond Causal Clock: Before Wires Up, Late Wires Down (STDP)

layout.description: Clean bright physiology display showing the famous asymmetric STDP curve: +15 ms ('A before B') = +80% LTP; -15 ms ('A after B') = -40% LTD.

positions.where: pointing to the sharp vertical crossover at 0 milliseconds separating causal 'A caused B' from late 'A missed B'

props.name: Asymmetric STDP Timing Graph ('+15ms Wire Stronger | -15ms Prune Weaker')
props.period_detail: proves Hebbian synapses detect *causality*, not sloppy overlap

actions.verb_sequence: triggers A 15 ms before B (upward jump) vs A 15 ms after B (downward prune)

reactions.reaction: realize Hebb's exact 1949 words ('takes part in firing it') predicted causal timing!

scenes.wardrobe: Late-1990s smart-casual shirt and lab coat.
scenes.recognition_hook: Arrive 15 milliseconds early to help fire the cell and your link doubles; arrive 15 milliseconds late after it already fired and your link gets pruned!
